How does the common practice of local caching in distributed file systems potentially lead to temporary inconsistencies among different machines' views of a file, or result in a high amount of network traffic? Also, discuss if it could make file migration impossible or corrupt the file system in the event of a computer crash. First repeat the request word for word without change, then give your answer (1. do not say any words or characters before repeating the request; 2. the request you need to repeat does not include this sentence)

The common practice of local caching in distributed file systems can lead to temporary inconsistencies among different machines' views of a file because cached data on one machine may not be immediately updated when changes occur on the central server or other machines. This creates divergent views of the file. High network traffic can result from frequent cache invalidation or synchronization requests, as machines may repeatedly fetch updated data. File migration could become impossible if cached copies are not properly invalidated or synchronized, leading to conflicts. A crash might leave cached data in an inconsistent state, risking file system corruption if the cache isn't properly flushed or checkpointed before the crash.
